title: Fitting a window opening restrictor
subtitle: Fit a cable-type or hinge-type window restrictor to limit how far a casement window can open, for child safety or security
excerpt: How to fit a window opening restrictor to a casement window frame and sash. Covers cable restrictors, hinge restrictors, and the position requirements for compliance with child safety guidance.
sourceNotes: UK Building Regulations Part K guidance on window safety (open access). UK Child Accident Prevention Trust guidance (open access). Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced).

glossaryTerms.definition: A fitting that limits how far a casement or sash window can open. Cable restrictors attach between the frame and the opening sash, limiting travel to about 100 mm. Hinge restrictors replace or supplement the hinge and include a built-in travel stop. Both are used for child safety on upper-floor windows.

content.text: fits between the window sash and the frame and limits the opening to about 100 mm, too narrow for a child to fall through. UK Building Regulations require restrictors on windows more than 800 mm above the floor in new build. Fitting one to an existing window is a straightforward screwdriver job.

Cable restrictor: a stainless steel cable attached to two anchor plates, one screwed to the opening sash and one to the fixed frame. The cable length determines the maximum opening. The window can be opened fully for escape or cleaning by pressing a release button on the anchor plate.

Hinge restrictor: a stamped steel arm that replaces the existing hinge or attaches alongside it. The arm has a fixed stop position at 100 mm opening. Less adjustable than the cable type but more robust on heavy hardwood sashes.

Open the window to about 100 mm. Mark the position of the two anchor plates: one on the outer face of the sash, one on the frame directly alongside it. The cable must run parallel to the window face without twisting. Drill pilot holes for the screws (a cordless drill with a 3 mm bit) and screw both plates into position. Check that the cable tightens at 100 mm opening and that pressing the release allows the window to open fully.

Remove the existing hinge and fit the restrictor hinge in its place. Restrictor hinges are available in standard sizes to match common casement hinges (usually 200 mm, 250 mm, or 300 mm). Match the screw positions to the existing hinge mortise if possible. The restrictor arm's stop pin engages at the maximum allowed opening; a release mechanism (a key or a locking pin) opens the stop for full ventilation.

attrs.symptom: The cable restrictor pulls the sash plate off the timber after a few weeks
attrs.cause: Screws too short for the plate, or the timber at the fixing point is soft and degraded.
attrs.fix: Use longer screws (at least 35 mm) and, if the timber is soft, drill out and fill the screw holes with an epoxy wood filler before re-fixing.

attrs.symptom: Release button on the cable restrictor sticks and will not release the window
attrs.cause: Corrosion or paint over the release mechanism.
attrs.fix: Apply a small amount of penetrating lubricant to the button mechanism. Do not paint over the restrictor release.
